newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil seen lower after Friday reverse.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil seen lower after Friday reverse.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil are expected to open weaker on Tuesday, taking their cue from an uninspired end to dealing last week when modest midsession gains on Friday turned into an 18-cent loss, dealers said.
June gas oil, which settled on Friday at $177.75 a tonne, was due to open about $1.50 lower while July Brent was expected to begin trading 15-20 cents below its close of $20.00 a barrel.
"There was a distinct lack of follow-through on Friday," said a broker.
"People were looking for a repeat of the previous week when the funds led it higher and it didn't happen," he said.
Both London and New York markets were closed on Monday for public holidays, with the U.S. marking Memorial Day which is traditionally seen as the start of the summer driving season.

But evidence the gasoline season may not live up to expectations was one of the reasons for the light profit taking and position squaring which dented sentiment ahead of the holiday weekend, dealers said.
"The funds are still in the money but there's a growing feeling that they may be long and wrong," said a broker.
NYMEX gasoline, which has led the market in recent days, shed 0.62 cent to 66.30 cents a gallon in ACCESS dealing.
American Petroleum Institute (API) data released last week showed U.S. gasoline stocks rose by 800,000 barrels but were still nearly seven million barrels below year ago levels.

European crude markets were still feeling the pressure of poor refining margins, in part due to a sharp rise in benchmark physical Dated Brent values, which could have more to do with a trader's derivatives strategy rather than fundamental strength.
